raw_response:
I'm a 37-year-old woman farming 16.1 mu of cotton here in Quzhou County, Hebei. I only finished primary school, and I've been back on the farm for 5 years — before that I worked in a garment factory in the city. My husband drives a delivery van part-time, my in-laws are getting old and can't do heavy work anymore, and I have two children in school. So most days the farming decisions fall on me, and I have to think carefully about every yuan because there's not much extra cash lying around.

I grow cotton on all 16.1 mu. Some neighbors switched to wheat-maize double cropping, but I don't know that system well and cotton has been okay for us. My mother-in-law says their family has grown cotton on this land for as long as she remembers, so I stick with what I know. Changing crops feels risky when you have children's school fees to pay.

For seeds, I buy hybrid Bt cotton from the county supply store — the ones with the pink coating. They cost about 90 yuan per mu, which is expensive, but three years ago I tried saving my own seed to save money. The bollworm ate almost a quarter of the crop and I lost way more than I saved. My neighbor Lao Zhang's wife did the same thing that year and had the same problem, so now we both buy new seed every year.

For fertilizer, I use three applications. Before planting in mid-to-late April, I spread about 30 kg of compound fertilizer per mu — the kind they call 15-15-15 at the shop. Then when the cotton starts flowering in early July, I topdress with about 10 kg of urea per mu. If the plants look strong and it rains well, I might add another 10 kg of urea in mid-August when the bolls are forming. Last year I skipped the August topdress to save about 300 yuan, and my yield dropped by maybe 20 kg per mu. My cousin's wife did all three applications and got a better crop, so this year I'm doing all three again. That's about 13 kg of nitrogen per mu total. I don't really think in kilograms — I know it as one bag of compound and two small bags of urea per mu — but the shopkeeper told me it's around that much.

Irrigation comes from our tube well. I plan to water twice this year: once at flowering in early July, and once at boll stage in mid-August. Three years ago I irrigated three times and the bill was too high — the electricity for pumping adds up fast on 16 mu. Two times seems to be enough if the summer rain is normal, and last year two times gave me 230 kg of lint per mu, which I can live with. My husband says I'm being too careful with the water bill, but he's not the one who has to find cash when the pump repair costs 500 yuan unexpectedly.

For pesticides, I spray herbicide once before planting to keep the weeds down — I learned that if you do it right before the cotton comes up, you don't need to spray again for weeds. Then for insects I spray insecticide four or five times through the summer. Even with Bt cotton we still get bollworm, especially in July and August. I use whatever the shop has in stock — last year it was something in a red bottle that cost about 20 yuan per mu per spray. I budget about 100 yuan per mu for chemicals for the season.

Tillage is simple — my husband plows once with our walking tractor in early April, then I go through and break up the big clods with a harrow. We don't have fancy equipment, but the walking tractor gets the job done. Then we plant by hand, row by row. It takes us about a week to get all 16 mu planted, working in the evenings after my husband gets back from his delivery route.

Labor is the hardest part of cotton. Planting, thinning, fertilizing, spraying, topping the plants in summer, and then picking — it's endless. My husband, my father-in-law (when his back allows), and I do most of the work. I figure we put in about 100 family days over the season. For picking, which happens in three rounds from September to October, I hire women from the village. Sixteen mu is too much for just family, and if you don't pick quickly the cotton gets dirty or wet. Last year I hired about 35 days of labor at 90 yuan per day. We pay by the day for picking, not by weight, because arguing over scales wastes time.

I'm expecting about 240 kg of lint per mu this year if the weather is normal. Last year I got 230 kg/mu, and the year before was 250 kg/mu. Cotton prices have been around 7-8 yuan per jin for seed cotton, so if I get 240 kg lint — that's roughly 600-650 jin of seed cotton per mu — we should have enough for the family and to pay the children's school fees in September. But I'm always a bit worried. If the price drops or if we get a dry August, the margin gets thin fast.

My total costs this year will be about 9,500 yuan. That's seed at 90 yuan/mu, fertilizer around 200 yuan/mu, irrigation pumping about 60 yuan/mu, pesticide about 100 yuan/mu, and hired labor about 200 yuan/mu. It's a lot of money for us, and some months I have to borrow from my sister until the cotton sells. But I've learned that skimping on fertilizer or pesticide costs you more in the end. I'd rather spend the money and have a safe crop than gamble and lose.
